model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Yakym: a heavily Republican district, incumbency, and a roughly 15-to-1 fundraising advantage, with markets pricing his win probability near 97%. With no polls or expert ratings to suggest movement, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based expectation of a mid-teens Republican margin.

overview:
Northern Indiana's 2nd District leans strongly Republican, and first-term incumbent Rudy Yakym is seeking a full term with the advantages of incumbency and a dominant fundraising operation. He has raised about $5.2 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Jamee Decio, who has raised roughly $356,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but lacks visible resources.

No public general-election polling or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, money, and market pricing, all of which favor Yakym heavily. Prediction markets put his win chances near 97 percent. The most plausible path for Decio would require a dramatic shift in the national environment or a surge of outside spending, neither of which is currently in evidence.
